Headline, dek and first three paragraphs I would publish, using only verified page content:

HEADLINE: Zionism, “through colonization.” Israel, “began committing genocide.” This is how Wikipedia now tells Israel’s story.

DEK: Since 2021 the first lines the world reads on Zionism, 1948, October 7 and Hamas have been rewritten. The hostages have never been in October 7’s first sentence.

P1: English Wikipedia’s Israel article, viewed 4.6 million times in the past 12 months, now says in Wikipedia’s own voice: “After the Hamas-led October 7 attacks, Israel began committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.” The sentence has stood since 4 May 2025; the next one reads: “Israel has denied that its actions constitute genocide.” In January 2021 and July 2023, none of the 150 most-read opening sections on the subject charged Israel with genocide.

P2: In January 2021, Zionism’s one-line definition spoke of “the re-establishment of and support for a Jewish state in the territory defined as the historic Land of Israel.” Since 27 August 2026 it has said “a Jewish homeland through colonization.” The Nakba, once “the destruction of Palestinian society,” is now “the ethnic cleansing of Palestinian Arabs by Zionists”; for the Jews who “fled or were expelled from Arab states,” no one is named. Hamas is “a political organisation with a military wing,” and its terror designation has moved from sentence 5 to sentence 22.

P3: October 7 itself is now “armed incursions” in its first sentence. Across 107 versions of that sentence, “massacre” lasted about an hour and the hostages never appeared; the openings of the Israel and Hamas articles do not mention them at all. Edits pushed both ways in similar numbers, but the critical wordings lasted about four times as long. Our tests found no sign of a large coordinated campaign, though a small one could slip through. This study measures what Wikipedia says, not whether it is true.
